posts.name: Gus_Smedstad
posts.cooked:
McBehrer:

Yeah, Benchmark is best hero

He's the New Standard™. Which is to say, the new baseline - other heroes can, of course, exceed that bar.

Kidding aside, my quick test game made him seem absurdly powerful. He's a bit dependent on setup, but he's functional WAY earlier than Absolute Zero or Bunker, the other two equipment-dependent heroes that come to mind. He's never going to deal out the sort of absurd damage Absolute Zero can when fully set up, or massively heal himself either, but he's more versatile and (as I said) much quicker off the starting blocks. As a power suit guy goes, I think he's just outright better than Bunker. About the only thing he's missing is anything equivalent to the Omni Cannon.

I played a game vs. Progeny using Benchmark, Stuntman and Knyfe and I had a lot bad luck. Stuntman and Knyfe were incapacitated and Benchmark at low health whereas Progeny was at 3/4 health but I still managed to win.

Sometimes Benchmark started his next turn with more health than his previous turn as he reduced all incoming damage by 1 and he healed at a lot of occasions 2 health. 

I never had a problem to have cards in my hand as he may draw a lot of them or get them back from his discard pile. I could play several cards and use 3 powers each turn.

Eypecially his Inferno Missile Pod had 10 cards and each dealt 1 damage which was buffed by +2. The missiles on their own are capable to deal 30 damage as he has a lot of possibilities to discard cards. An environment card even reduced the fire damage of the missiles by 1 but Progeny was utterly destroyed (look at the picture I posted).

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
MigrantP:

Version 2.6 with Mini-Pack 4 is now available on Amazon Appstore. I know it can take some time for the Appstore to update automatically, but it's there! https://www.amazon.com/Handelabra-Studio-LLC-Sentinels-Multiverse/dp/B00…

It was actually up Saturday morning.  Had to clear my Amazon app data to force the download, but I've played a mess of games so far.

Something I wasn't expecting: the word I'd most use to define both new heroes is "inconsistent."

Benchmark has so many unique cards, he can never be sure of getting anything in particular.  Every game with him will be very different; it's hard to use a strategy in advance.  Sometimes you get nice combos, sometimes you don't.  Thematically it makes sense–he's sort of an Inspector Gadget-type, with a lot of useful tools but not a lot of experience–but it can be frustrating at times.  It does add replay value, though.

Stuntman is heavily dependent on getting either Lance-Flammes or Pistolet-Mitralleur.  His base power has its uses, but is usually vastly inferior to those.  Sky-Scraper and her Micro-Assembler can be his best friends.  He also has a lot of cool things to do that may or may not be what you really want.  I've only drawn In Medias Res three times out of a dozen or so games, and in none of them was I able to use it to particularly good effect.  So he's also very swingy–can be a lot of fun but is often just going through the motions.
